content.value: `api_tokens` rows with sha256-hashed secrets and `read`/`write`/`admin` permissions — the guard in front of every HTTP API v1 route.
rows. The raw secret is never stored; Barkpark keeps
as a hex hash and compares hashes on every request. Each row carries a permission level —
— that decides which HTTP API v1 verbs the holder may call. This is the gate the whole of Barkpark sits behind.
— there is no Workspace or Project membership check. Hold a

token and you can write into the default scope. This is deliberate: it keeps the Bulldocs paper-ingest and Tasks Plugin task-create paths simple, and it is why a Webhooks row must explicitly carry the default workspace/project to fire on those flat mutations.
Tokens also key what the Capabilities Manifest reveals. A lower-tier token doesn't merely get
on routes it can't reach — those routes are

from its manifest, so it cannot tell whether they exist. Existence-hiding closes the enumeration vector that a plain permission error would leak, and it applies identically to data reads and to capabilities discovery.
The bp CLI and Go TUI read a token from config; the JS SDK and Web Demo carry one server-side. The same hash check protects Postgres Search queries and Content Edges Table graph reads.
